body: ## What An opt-in numerics tier for the MoE expert passes of a one-lane decode step: `splash serve --moe-numerics fast` (default `invariant`). Under it, a one-lane DFlash verify step (8 rows, read in place since #365) runs each routed expert that takes at most R of the step's rows through a register GEMV on those rows alone, and every other expert, and the shared expert always, through the unchanged 8-row staged tile. ## Why Since #365 a one-lane step's rows are read in place: one 8-row tile per expert, and each tile runs the 8-row `matmul2d` whatever rows route to its expert. On 320 real one-lane DFlash steps of a 256-expert, top-8 target (hidden 2048, expert width 512), 54% of the experts take one of the 8 rows, 23% two, 10% three; the mean is 2.0. The staged tile pays the same dequantization, stage, barrier and 8-row matmul for one row as for eight. A register GEMV dequantizes each weight once into registers and multiplies it with the live rows only, so its cost grows with the rows; for one-row experts it is cheaper than the staged tile in every format measured. ## Scope - Only one-lane decode plans on the staged tile (`MoePlan::smallTilesInPlace`: Fast numerics, decode phase, `rowsInPlace()`): Apple10 and later. Wider steps (B=2-4), every prefill chunk (the 8-row chunk too), Apple9's register tile and dense projections run the default kernels under either tier. - Default tier: the default kernels' source is unchanged (the Fast kernels are separate entry points); the grouping kernel only gains a branch for the new `in_place` value. Measured below: same speed and same greedy outputs as `be3b083`. - B>1 is excluded for numerics policy, not speed: there a row's path would depend on other requests' routes. ## Design - **In place kept.** `MoeGroupParams::in_place` 2 (same 28-byte layout): the grouping writes each routed tile's live-row count into its descriptor and the plan rows of its routes into the routed tile's otherwise unused `groupedRoutes` slots: 64 more stores per layer in a dispatch that already runs. No new dispatch, buffer or grid; the live-tile indirect grids of #345 are unchanged. - **One dispatch per pass, per-threadgroup branch.** `moe_expert_gguf_fast_m8_gate_up` (one pass, #345's shape) and `moe_expert_gguf_fast_m8_{a,g}` (two-format gate/up and down) bind the live-row list after the default bindings. A tile of a routed expert with at most `MoeGgufExpertParams::gemv_rows` live rows runs the GEMV; any other tile runs the default kernels' tile body, so its outputs are bitwise the default tier's. The branch is uniform per threadgroup. Threadgroup memory is the default kernels' 9 KB: the GEMV never stages, so the 8 KB stage holds a grid format's grid (all of IQ2_S's 1024 entries), the pair table a codebook format's table, and either one part's partial sums. - **GEMV** (`kernels/common/gguf_live_rows.h`). Each weight is dequantized as `dequant32` rounds it for the stage (each value once to half), so half x bf16 products are exact in fp32 and the GEMV differs from the staged tile only in fp32 summation order. One fixed sum order per row and column: K's groups in two interleaved parts, each summed in ascending order into a float4 and reduced as (x + y) + (z + w), the parts added in order. The one-pass gate/up runs one part per simdgroup, lane l owning column l of both gate and up (one read of the input row per group for both tensors); the other passes run lane = column over all of K. Both forms give the same bits, so gguf-moe's one-pass-vs-two-pass equality also holds for the Fast tier. Rows are read in place through the live-row list (16-byte input loads), payloads of the next groups load while the current ones multiply. - **R per pass by routed format** (`moe_fast_gemv_rows`, ABI header, shared by host and kernels): 1 for IQ2_S/IQ2_XS/IQ2_XXS, IQ3_S/IQ3_XXS, IQ4_XS, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0 and for Q4_K down; 2 for Q4_K gate/up. Formats without a GEMV (0) keep the default kernels for that pass. Values come from the microbench sweep below; two-row GEMV tiles lose to the staged tile except for Q4_K gate/up. - **Host.** `MoeNumerics { BatchInvariant, Fast }` on `MoeConfig`; `ExecutionPlans(device, moeNumerics)`; `NativeArguments::moeNumerics` from `serve-native --moe-numerics invariant|fast`; `splash serve --moe-numerics` (server option, native command golden line). Upstream reads no runtime environment knobs, so this is an engine flag rather than an env var; happy to change the spelling or where it lives. The engine logs one line at startup when Fast is on. ## Numbers 16-core M5 Pro (Apple10), 1619-1620 MHz in every sampled slot, AC, no thermal or performance warnings, no swap-outs. **Microbench**, one MoE layer per call through `MoE::add` (router to combine), real routing of 320 one-lane DFlash verify steps replayed through an identity router, 40 layers per command over 4 weight copies (DRAM-cold), 2 rounds x 9 repeats, us per layer (mean of rounds). "Staged branch" is the Fast kernels with R = 0, every tile on the default body: | gate/up / down / shared formats | default tier | Fast (R gate/up:down) | saved | gate/up pass | down pass | staged branch (R 0:0) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | IQ2_S / IQ3_S / Q6_K | 297.97 | 280.53 (1:1) | -17.4 (-5.9%) | -9.8 | -9.6 | +2.5 (+0.8%) | | IQ2_S / IQ4_XS / Q6_K | 300.47 | 279.47 (1:1) | -21.0 (-7.0%) | -11.5 | -11.8 | +1.7 (+0.6%) | | Q4_K / Q5_K / Q8_0 | 302.54 | 293.73 (2:1) | -8.8 (-2.9%) | -12.4 | -5.0 | +1.1 (+0.4%) | | Q4_K / Q6_K / Q8_0 | 314.53 | 306.22 (2:1) | -8.3 (-2.6%) | -12.4 | -4.3 | +0.6 (+0.2%) | Threshold sweep, IQ2_S / IQ3_S (saved us per layer, R gate/up:down): 1:0 -5.0, 0:1 -7.5, 0:2 -2.6, 1:1 -16.7, 1:2 -11.9, 2:1 -10.4, 2:2 -6.0. **Served A/B**, `splash serve` (`--max-cache-disk 0 --idle-release off`), DFlash, one request at a time, 24 prompts x 256 greedy tokens per server start, ABBA rounds (a server start per slot, weights page-cached), mean +- 95% CI over rounds; cycle GPU ms from `/status` model timing, tau = tokens per DFlash cycle; A/A null = last A slot / first A slot of each round: | target experts (gate/up, down), rounds | metric | invariant | fast | fast / invariant (paired) | A/A null | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | IQ2_S, IQ3_S (IQ4_XS on 3 layers), 5 | tok/s | 174.70 +- 0.49 | 180.34 +- 0.56 | **1.0323 +- 0.0017** | +0.19 +- 0.52% | | | cycle GPU ms | 24.325 +- 0.056 | 23.462 +- 0.100 | **0.9645 +- 0.0035** | -0.09 +- 0.26% | | | tau | 4.220 | 4.191 | 0.9932 | | | Q4_K, Q5_K (Q6_K on 3 layers), 3 | tok/s | 172.25 +- 0.26 | 175.74 +- 0.06 | **1.0203 +- 0.0014** | +0.07 +- 0.11% | | | cycle GPU ms | 25.353 +- 0.041 | 24.934 +- 0.009 | **0.9835 +- 0.0014** | -0.07 +- 0.15% | | | tau | 4.300 | 4.342 | 1.0099 | | Default tier against `be3b083` (IQ2_S/IQ3_S target, 3 ABBA rounds): tok/s 175.01 +- 0.19 vs 174.94 +- 0.08, ratio 0.9996 +- 0.0015; cycle GPU 1.0004 +- 0.0016 (A/A -0.07 +- 0.14%); tau 4.220 both; greedy outputs identical on all 24 prompts in every run (144/144). ## Numerics - Not batch-invariant, hence opt-in: an expert's path depends on how many of the step's 8 rows route to it, so a row's MoE output depends on the draft tokens verified with it, and differs from the same token in a prefill chunk or a wider step. - Deterministic for a step's routes: the path is a function of the counts, each row's sum order is fixed, and the one atomic (the live-row slot) does not enter the arithmetic. Served: no fast run's greedy output differed from the first fast run's (0 of 240 and 0 of 144 prompt runs). - Inside the same fp64 bound as the staged tile (half-rounded weights, exact products, fp32 sums). gguf-moe (shader validation) runs the Fast tier's one-lane plan for every staged format pair, one-pass and two-format gate/up, on routes made to give experts 1, 2, 3 and 8 rows: every pass inside the fp64 interval, the live-row grouping (counts, each row listed once, nothing past them), one pass bitwise two passes, live grids bitwise full grids, a second run bitwise the first, the shared expert's rows bitwise the default tier's, outputs bitwise the default tier's where no pass takes the GEMV, and B2/B4 decode and 8/27-row prefill plans under Fast pick the default kernels; 0.00-0.12% of the block's outputs differ from the default tier. gguf-dequant checks the register dequantization (`dequant32_values`, and the threadgroup grid copies) against the half rounding of every reference weight. execution-plans pins where the tier applies. - Served greedy text differs from the default tier on 21 of 24 prompts (IQ2_S/IQ3_S target) and 20 of 24 (Q4_K/Q5_K target); tau moves -0.7% and +1.0%. - Perplexity equivalence, pre-registered before any data (margin 0.001 nats/token; pass iff the upper bound of the 95% t-CI of the paired mean per-window dNLL < 0.001): all 145 wikitext-2 test windows x 2048 tokens (296,815 scored tokens), teacher-forced in 8-row chunks through the one-lane decode step's MoE plan (a local harness lets the Fast tier take the 8-row in-place chunk, whose MoE plan is the decode step's; not part of this PR). dNLL (fast - invariant) **+0.000235 nats/token, 95% CI [-0.000374, +0.000844]: PASS**; 80 windows up, 65 down, max |d| 0.0143; PPL 7.1312 vs 7.1329. ## Relation to other PRs - #345 (one-pass gate/up, live-tile grids): kept; the Fast gate/up is one pass with #345's grid, and the GEMV keeps one read of the input for gate and up. - #365 (in-place one-lane plan): kept; this builds on it (the live-row list lets the GEMV read the plan's rows in place, so no gather comes back). - #367 (live-row expert passes on Apple9): the same core mechanism, a different policy (Apple9's every decode tile over gathered rows, eight K parts; here Apple10's few-row tiles in place, the 8-row matmul kept for the rest). Rather than a second implementation, `kernels/common/gguf_live_rows.h` holds #367's `dequant32_values` and a generalization of its `moe_rows_pass` walk (parts of K as a template parameter, several column streams per lane, in-place row offsets, an optional threadgroup grid); #367 could take it with eight parts. If #367 merges first I will rebase onto it and keep only the generalization. - #443 (ours, prefill shared expert): textual conflicts in `ops/MoE.{hpp,cpp}`, `abi/MoE.h`, `moe.metal` and `gguf_moe_test.mm`; layouts are compatible (`MoeGroupParams` keeps its layout here, #443 appends `shared_base`). This PR conflicts textually with #443 and #367 and will be rebased on whichever merges first. ## Caveats - Measured on one GPU (16-core M5 Pro); the thresholds are that GPU's. Other Apple10+ configurations may want other R. - The staged branch of the Fast kernels costs +0.7-1.0% of the gate/up pass against the default kernel (cause not isolated); it is included in every Fast number above. - The persistent prefix cache is not keyed on the tier, as it is not on the Neural Engine split: KV written by Fast verify steps may be reused by a later invariant process with `--persistent-cache`. The runtime oracle (#428) should run the default tier. - Not measured: tile-order variants (small tiles last), R = 8 on Apple10 (#367's every-tile policy), M=16/32 plans. Tests: `make check-source check-native-cpu check-native-build`, `MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1 make check-native-metal`, `dev/tests/server/test_serve_options.py` pass. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_012gTpeJqYXcXA8LvLavka8w --- Need help on this PR?
